answer_text:
Let \(f:\mathbb{Q}\to \mathbb{Z}\) be a group homomorphism of additive abelian groups.

For any \(q\in \mathbb{Q}\) and any positive integer \(n\), we have \(q/n\in \mathbb{Q}\). Since \(f\) is additive,

\[
f(q)=f(n\cdot (q/n))=n f(q/n).
\]

Because \(f(q/n)\in \mathbb{Z}\), this means \(f(q)\) is divisible by every positive integer \(n\).

The only integer divisible by every positive integer is \(0\). Hence

\[
f(q)=0 \qquad \text{for all } q\in \mathbb{Q}.
\]

Therefore every homomorphism \(\mathbb{Q}\to \mathbb{Z}\) is the zero homomorphism. Thus

\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{Z}) \cong 0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
